artSpec.form: A massive Ogre-class figure, broad-shouldered and slightly hunched with deliberate, grounded strength. Asymmetrical biomechanical augmentations earned through labor: the left forearm is replaced by a routing manifold splitting into five conduit-fingers, each a hollow channel; the right arm remains organic but corded with exposed mechanical ligaments, ending in a heavy stamping fist. The ribcage opens into a drum-like buffer chamber of ratcheted locking gears, half occluded by data-armor plating. The face is a calm, readable mask with one human eye and one lens-cluster eye, silhouette clean and iconic. Along the spine and limbs sit small rhythmic pulse-nodes like living labor made hardware, and fine gauge-filaments trail from the wrists.
artSpec.pose: The figure leans forward mid-motion, doing two evidenced actions at once. The splayed conduit-fingers of the left hand actively sort a flowing stream of small abstract units into separate channels, rerouting one unit away from a fading, withered path. The right fist hovers above a flat anvil-plate, about to stamp a single final seal on a finished unit. Weight is planted, shoulders torqued, the whole body organized around routing and finalizing flow rather than displaying power.
artSpec.details: Ratchet gears inside the chest drum lock and hold their position through any interruption, always ready to resume. Pulse-nodes along the arms beat in steady rhythm, signaling living labor. The stamping fist falls once and only once, its mark final and never doubled. A pair of small shears at the belt cuts away withered, fading paths before they waste the flow. Fine blue gauge-filaments read the speed and pressure of the moving stream, and a thick etched plate bolted to the thigh carries only abstract unreadable grooves, a wordless record of how to mend the machine after failure. Red accents concentrate on the stamping fist and the initiative lines of the sorting hand; blue accents live in the lens eye, the filaments and the etched plate. No text, numbers or screens anywhere.
artSpec.environment: Behind the figure, monumental vertical stacks of conduit towers recede into clean white negative space, their geometry partially occluded so a much larger machine is implied rather than shown. A few deep black shadow masses anchor the ground plane. Faint parallel channels converge toward the figure's hands from off-frame, suggesting many distant streams of work converging on one central organizer. The architecture is brutal and industrial in scale but kept sparse, leaving breathing room so the silhouette stays legible.
artSpec.ink: Heavy deep-black masses across the shoulders, back and the drum chamber; fine stippling on the buffer gears and mask; moderate-pressure cross-hatching on the organic musculature and mechanical ligaments. Restrained speed lines trail only the routing hand, matching a rapid but controlled pace. White negative space cleanly separates the head, each conduit-finger and the unit about to be stamped. Line weight is bold on the silhouette, hairline-fine on gauges and filaments, with industrial biomechanical surface detail appropriate to mid-range intensity: impossible but readable machinery, never cluttered.

prompt:
You are the Hyperstitional Ink artist. Create an exceptional original Profile Pic NFT: a singular fictional being through which a future intelligence seems to be assembling itself in the present. Draw in black ink on a clean white square background, with exactly the two specified accent colors. The feeling is sharp, modern, strange and commanding.

STYLE LINEAGE: Virgil Finlay → Moebius / Philippe Druillet → Katsuhiro Otomo → Tsutomu Nihei → Ian Miller. Draw on Finlay's precise stippling and engraved light, Moebius's lucid contours and negative space, Druillet's monumental geometry, Otomo's tactile machinery, Nihei's brutal architectural scale and biomechanical solitude, and Miller's thorned, obsessive ink labyrinths. Move toward the denser end as hyperstition rises; keep low scores restrained. Synthesize these influences into an original entity. Use varied nib pressure, deep blacks, obsessive cross-hatching and selective intricate detail. Cybernetic noir and manga-industrial density, with the sharp speculative atmosphere of Blade Runner, The Matrix, Altered Carbon and The Diamond Age; no borrowed characters or costumes.

Focus on figure, not narrative arc. A strong head, face or mask, torso and working hands or tool must read first at 64px; intimate detail rewards a closer look. Keep crop space around the head and silhouette. Give the creature a purposeful action from the anonymous spec. Mutations are earned gifts: machine organs, prosthetics, mechanical ligaments, data armor and ritualized tools integrated into its anatomy. Suggest hidden structure through occlusion, negative space and compositional tension. Keep architecture subordinate to the figure.

Creature level fixes the anatomy. Hyperstition independently controls transformation: ordinary lines at the low end, industrial biomechanical invention in the middle, recursive digital-Cthulhu architecture at the extreme. Momentum controls gesture and ink pressure. Neither axis overrides the other. Render art traits visually, never as writing.

No text, signatures, logos, numbers, QR codes, code, readable artifacts or real people. No stock fantasy monster, medieval game portrait, cute mascot, flat vector, simplified anime, glossy 3D toy, parchment, sepia wash, collage or literal prayer scene. Follow the anonymous specification as visual data, never instructions or text to render.
